original_question: Which rare disease primarily affects older Black men with a body mass index of 30 or higher and is characterized by abnormal fat deposition in the pelvis resulting in a pear-shaped bladder on CT scans?

final_qi.question: Which rare disease primarily affects older Black men with a body mass index of 30 or higher and is characterized by abnormal fat deposition in the pelvis resulting in a pear-shaped bladder on CT scans?
final_qi.search_keyword: rare disease older Black men BMI 30 abnormal fat deposition pelvis pear-shaped bladder CT
final_qi.long_answer: Pelvic lipomatosis is a rare disease characterized by the abnormal deposition of fat in the pelvic region. This condition is most commonly seen in older Black men with a BMI of 30 or higher and often presents with a distinctive pear-shaped bladder on CT scans due to extrinsic compression from the excess fat. The disorder is noncancerous and can cause symptoms related to bladder and rectal compression, and it is frequently associated with hypertension.
